1
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell:

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 19.11.2021 at about 12.00 p.m when the petitioner was walking on the main road, at 6th Cross, near Muddannanagalli at that time the driver of Tata Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-B-1235 which is came from reverse in rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life, lost control and dashed the petitioner.
As a result of impact, petitioner fell down and sustained injuries all over the body.
It is urged that the petitioner has spent more than Rs.3 lakhs towards his treatment and medical expenses.

It is urged that as on the date of accident he was hale and healthy and was doing business and earning more than Rs.50,000/- p.m and due to the accidental injuries he unable to work as such he suffered both financially and emotionally.

Further it is specifically urged that,
the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata Goods vehicle as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation as such prayed to allow the petition.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.

4. After service of notice respondent No.2 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tata XL vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-B-1235.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
Further the respondent No.2 has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory Section 147, 149, 134(c) and 158 (6) of M.V.Act.
The respondent claim right U/Sec.170 of M.V.Act. Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the car did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 19.11.2021 at about 12.00 p.m, near Magadi road 6th Cross,
Muddannanagalli, Bengaluru City, due to actionable negligence on the part of the Mahabaleshwara M.S vs Umesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82747784/
2 driver of Tata Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-B- 1235 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .P1 to 20 were marked on his behalf.
The MRT of Apollo Hospital was examined as PW.2.
Ex's .P21 to 25 were marked through this witness.

Dr.B.
Ramesh, Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital was examined as PW.3.
Ex's .P26 & 27 were marked through him.
The respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence on its behalf.
7. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:
The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in the RTA.
The case of the petitioner lies an narrow compass as to claiming of compensation amount for injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident.
Before dwelling into analyzing the disputed facts in issue it is relevant to have the birds eye of the case of petitioner in a nutshell.

Further it is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata Goods vehicle as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation as such prayed to allow the petition.
11. In support of case of petitioner herself stepped into the witness box and filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in- chief as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P20 documents.

Added more the doctor who was assessed the disability is examined as PW.3 and through him Ex.P.26 & 27 are marked.
In order to falsify the case of the petitioner and to substantiate the defence of the respondent no.2, their counsel had cross-
examined PW1 to Pw3 at length.
12. Repelling to the contentions urged by the petitioner, the respondent No.2 had attacked the case of the petitioner on various prisms known to fact and law.
The first and foremost contention urged by the respondent is that, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle.
It is also urged that the driver of the Tempo was not having valid DL at the time of driving the vehicle.
It is specifically contended that there is no nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Further denied all the allegations made in the petition.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
13. In order to substantiate the above said factum the respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence.

14. On marshaling of factual matrix, on dissection of evidence placed on record and after hearing on erudite counsel appearing for petitioner and respondent, this court opines that both the rival parties are at the logger heads on the factum of negligence.
It is specifically urged by the petitioner that the driver of the insured tempo is negligent and as a result of which the accident occurred.
When such being the case the specific contentions urged by the rival parties it is relevant to fall back about the documentary and oral evidence in this regard.
The petitioner has mainly relied on Ex.P.1 to 8 documents being the police documents to prove the factum of negligence.
Negligence has to be proved as a matter of fact.
15. Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.

Mahabaleshwara M.S vs Umesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82747784/
4 Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

16. Reverting back to the factual matrix it is specifically urged by the petitioner that the driver of the Tata goods vehicle while taking the reverse without taking due care and caution had hit the petitioner.
In support of the case the wife of the petitioner has set criminal law into motion by filing Ex.P.2 on the very same day of accident.
The FIR as its germane in its to Ex.P.2 complaint.
Further more one of the documents which sheds light on the factum of rash and negligence manner is ExP.4 being the crime details form and sketch appended to the said document.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that the vehicle while taking the reverse had hit the petitioner.
This factums itself speaks volumes as to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the vehicle.
Further more it is contended that the driver of the Tata goods vehicle was not having valid DL.
It is pertinent to note that IO has given Notice u/s 133 of IMV Act as per Ex.P.7 and the said notice was replied as per Ex.P.8 wherein the DL number was mentioned.
Added more there are no materials was placed by the respondent No.2 in order to buttress his claim that the driver of the tempo was having valid DL.
Hence the contention urged by the respondent No.2 does not hold any water in the eye of law.
17. Furthermore even the charge sheet is filed as against the driver of the Tempo this also remains unchallenged and undenied.
This court is aware of the fact the chargesheet cannot be trusted as a holy document to come to the conclusion of the negligence.

But in the instant case having regard to the other materials placed on record and other surrounding circumstances it is it is clearly forthcoming that the negligence on the part of the driver of the Tata Tempo.
Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Tempo.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
18. ISSUE NO.2 :

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injury : (i)
Blunt trauma chest, (ii) bilateral hemopnenmothorax with diffuse, (iii) subautaneous emplhysema,
(iv) bilateral ICD insertion, left 2 nd and 3rd rib anterio lateral fracture.
It is needless to say that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

The discharge summary issued by Apollo hospital, Nelamangala indicate that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 19.11.2021 to 29.11.2021 (11 days in total).

Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
19. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD :
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries she has become disabled and lost her earning capacity.

Mahabaleshwara M.S vs Umesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82747784/
5

Therefore she got examined Dr.B. Ramesh as PW.3, who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has total permanent physical disability of the right upper limb at 17% and whole body disability at 6%.
It is elicited during the course of cross-examination that PW.3 is not a treated doctor.
Further it is categorically admitted that the petitioner has taken conservative treatment.
Further it is also admitted that malunion of fracture is not mentioned in the follow up records.
20. It is relevant to note that, Clavicle bone means (collarbone) is a long, slightly curved bone that connects your arm to your body.
The said bone can be found one on both sides of the base of the neck.
The bones help keep a shoulder blade in the correct position as a person move.
The word "clavicle" comes from the Latin "clavicula," which translates to "little key."
The bone is actually shaped a bit like an old-fashioned key.
And it works in much the same way.
When one rotate a key, it moves the lock.
Similarly, when a person lift a arm, a clavicle rotates along its axis to allow movement.
The clavicle, or collarbone, is a slender, S-shaped long bone approximately 6 inches (15 cm) long that serves as a strut between the shoulder blade and the sternum (breastbone).
There are two clavicles, one on the left and one on the right.
The clavicle is the only long bone in the body that lies horizontally.
Together with the shoulder blade, it makes up the shoulder girdle.
It is a palpable bone and, in people who have less fat in this region, the location of the bone is clearly visible.
It receives its name from Latin clavicula 'little key' because the bone rotates along its axis like a key when the shoulder is abducted.
The clavicle is the most commonly fractured bone.
It can easily be fractured by impacts to the shoulder from the force of falling on outstretched arms or by a direct hit.
21. It is relevant to note that, Clavicle or collar bone is a slender S shaped bone approximately 6 inches that serves as a strut between the shoulder blade and the sternum.
Together with the shoulder blade, it makes up the shoulder griddle.
To put it differently, clavicle bone is not a separate component of the arm but just a supporting bone.
It is in this view of the matter, no disability is prescribed for clavicle fracture in the Government of India guidelines 2018.
Despite of it, PW.3 has assessed the whole body disability of the petitioner at 6% which is totally contrary to the guidelines.
Be that as it may as the clavicle fracture does not lead to any disability the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
22. Further it is to be seen whether the aforesaid disability impairs the avocation of the petitioner.

As per the averments made in his evidence affidavit prior to the accident he was doing service of designing of object and offset printing in Bengaluru and had earning Rs.50,000/- p.m. During the course of cross examination that as here under : "It is true to suggest that I have declare higher income in Ex.P.15 then income at the time of accident".
This categorical admission of PW1 himself goes to show that, there is no loss of future income.

Further it could be ascertained from the materials placed on record and the admission of PW.l himself that at the time of accident he was earning Rs.50,000/- p.m but he declare higher income in Ex.P.15 then income at the time of accident.
Mahabaleshwara

6
Further it could be be ascertained from the documentary as well as oral evidence that, petitioner has not suffered any loss of income after the accident.
Infact the petitioner is getting the higher income then prior to the accident.
Further he had also not produced bank account statement to show that he was not earning any income during laid up period but for the best reasons known to him he failed to produce the same.

In this regard reliance is placed upon the decision reported in AIR 1964 SC 136 wherein it is held that '(e) Evidence Act (1872), S.114 - All relevant documents admitted to have been in existence not placed before Court by party concerned - Adverse inference has to be drawn against party.'
23.

It is specifically urged by the petitioner by placing reliance on Ex.P.20 Visual disability certificate issued by Udaya Ravi Eye hospital stating that the petitioner has sustained visual disability to the tune of 30%.
It is relevant to note that, there is no pleading with regard to eye injury.
Further more the wound certificate and discharge summary also does not spells out with regard to eye injury.
The wound certificate and discharge summary does not even have any reference with regard to eye injury.
It is pertinent to note that, even the petitioner did not sustain head injury also.
This factum is categorically admitted by PW.1 himself during the course of cross examination.
Added more Ex.P.11 is certificate issued by Udaya Ravi Eye Hospital dated 22.12.2022.
The said certificate is issued with related to the treatment taken by the petitioner in the said hospital.
On perusal of the said document it reflects that, the petitioner had taken treatment after the lapse of one year from the date of injury.
Another important aspect which this court does not loose sight fact that, the petitioner had not examined the Optomologist in order to substantiate his claim with regard to eye injury.
24. It is canvassed vociferously by learned counsel for the petitioner by placing reliance on on Purtcher's retinopathy.
The stout arguments canvassed by relying on the various literature with regard to opthomology.
This court gave anxious consideration to the said literature and case study.
On careful perusal of the same it reflects that in the above said literature depicts upon eye disability and also sustained head injury or spinal cord injury,.
In the above said literature it is made crystal clear that the patient sustained spine injury which is the central part of sending messages to brain to all sensory organs.
If the spine gets damaged then it will cause impairement to the eye.
In the instant case on hand neither the spine nor the head injury is stained by the petitioner.
When such being the case merely because of some stray entry in Ex.P.20 wherein whose author is also not examined, the Ex.P.20 cannot be trusted as gospel truth.
25. The discussion supra goes to show petitioner has not suffered any financial loss during the laid-up period.
Non- production of these documents leads to drawing of an adverse inference that the petitioner has continued carrying on his business.
Meaning thereby he has not sustained any financial loss on account of the accidental injuries suffered by him.

Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
26.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The period of hospitalization of 11 days is proved.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would Mahabaleshwara M.S vs Umesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82747784/
7 have accompanied her to the hospital to take him care by leaving their duties.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,500/- per day and a sum of Rs.16,500/- (1,500 X 11) is awarded under this head.
27. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
28. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the bills marked at Ex.P13, the petitioner has spent Rs.5,42,024/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of her cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,42,024/- which is rounded off to Rs.5,42,000/- towards medical expenses.
29. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.60,000/- is awarded under this head.
30. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.
31. The calculation table stands as follows:

1 Loss of future income due to : - Nil - disability 2 Loss of income during laid-up : - Nil - period 3 Attendant charges, extra : 16,500-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 4 Pain & sufferings : 60,000-00 5
Medical expenses : 5,42,000-00 6 Loss of future amenities & : 60,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : - Nil - Total 6,78,500-00 32.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
33. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Tata Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-B-1235 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable Mahabaleshwara M.S vs Umesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82747784/
8 to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
34. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,78,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
